issues.description: PR title and CHANGELOG say compute_image_not_publicly_shared but description says compute_image_publicly_shared — pick one and make the tree match
issues.detail: The PR description body says the directory is compute_image_publicly_shared/. The actual diff creates compute_image_not_publicly_shared/. This kind of sloppiness in the commit message is exactly what wastes a maintainer's time. Fix the description or fix the path, but don't ship both names.

issues.description: Image listing is not threaded like every other resource in this service — inconsistent with surrounding code
issues.detail: Every other collection in compute_service.py uses __threading_call__ over projects/regions/zones. _get_images iterates project_ids serially in the constructor. Match the existing style of the surrounding code, or have a specific technical reason not to. Right now it just looks like the author didn't read the file they were editing.

issues.description: images().list(project=project_id) returns Google-public images too, not just custom ones — check will spam findings
issues.detail: The GCP images.list call without filtering returns the project's own images, but a real concern is whether deprecated/family/public images leak in depending on filter. The description claims this only evaluates custom images, but there is no filter=deprecated.state!=DEPRECATED or similar in the code. State the filter explicitly or document why none is needed.

issues.description: Exception handler reads error.__traceback__.tb_lineno which can be None and crash the error handler itself
issues.detail: If the exception has no traceback attached (rare but happens with re-raised or constructed exceptions), tb_lineno access on None will throw inside the except block and you lose the original error entirely. The rest of this file uses the same pattern, so it's a repo-wide issue, but copying a buggy pattern into new code is not a defense. Use traceback.format_exc() or guard it.

issues.description: Test for IAM-policy exception path asserts publicly_shared=False, masking the failure instead of surfacing it
issues.detail: test-image-3 triggers an Exception in getIamPolicy and the test asserts publicly_shared is False. That means a permission-denied error silently produces a PASS finding. That's a bad-taste failure mode: an auth error becomes a clean bill of health. At minimum, log-and-skip rather than log-and-pass, or mark the image as unknown.

issues.description: Image model has no location/self_link/source-project fields — minimal but probably too minimal for a finding report
issues.detail: Other models in this file carry self_link, region, etc. A finding on a shared image with only name+id+project_id may be hard to act on if the same name exists in multiple projects or families. Not a blocker, but the next maintainer will add fields one at a time and curse the original patch.

review.summary: The patch does one thing, which is good. But it doesn't match the voice of the file it's editing — every other resource in compute_service.py is collected via __threading_call__, and this one isn't. The PR description and the actual directory name disagree (compute_image_publicly_shared vs compute_image_not_publicly_shared); pick one. The IAM-policy exception path silently produces PASS findings, which is bad taste — an auth failure should not look like a clean image. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK. Fix the threading, fix the name mismatch, and decide what a permission error means before merging.
